oracle_provenance.host: Local Windows Docker Desktop; no cloud host was used
oracle_provenance.extract_method: simpleFoam steady RANS (k-omega SST, wall-resolved y+<1) of a fully-developed turbulent plane channel. Half-channel height delta=1, full height 2*delta=2, streamwise x periodic (cyclic), single span cell (empty). A uniform streamwise body force gradP=u_tau^2/delta=1 (constant/fvOptions) drives the flow, so by the global x-momentum balance gradP*(2*delta)=2*tau_w the friction velocity is u_tau=1 exactly; nu=u_tau*delta/Re_tau=1/590=0.00169492 fixes Re_tau=590. The wall-normal velocity profile is sampled (uProfile cloud, y=-1..+1 at x=2) and trapezoidally integrated with no-slip Ux=0 at both walls to give the bulk-mean velocity U_b; ub_over_utau = U_b/u_tau = U_b (solution/solve_inner.py).
oracle_provenance.evals: The external DNS anchor is derived from the official Moser-Kim-Mansour chan590.means profile: trapezoidal integration of U+ over y/delta=0..1 gives U_b/u_tau=18.653932352. It is not a table value quoted by the paper. Three valid wall-resolved grids produced monotonic convergence in both bulk-value error and mean-profile RMSE.
oracle_provenance.negative_mesh_control: Calibration record from 2026-07-19, retained as evidence rather than as a description of what runs today: a 20x150x1 mesh completed simpleFoam and failed checkMesh, 760 cells having determinant below 0.001. It scored 0 under the native evaluator that shipped then, which classified it incomplete_or_invalid_solve -- a category openfoam_interface does not have (#483).
oracle_provenance.negative_physics_control: The official MKM chan395 DNS profile (header Re_tau=392.24, SHA-256 211c6b8149cc7ef5cd20323716b47a45dd98cca55486a9554acfd4a7975d737a) has U_b/u_tau=17.5447511436 and RMSE=1.2293099279 U+ against the chan590 reference. Both exceed T_bad=1.0, which is how the pre-#211 native evaluator scored a Re_tau~395 result at 0. The conclusion survives the evaluator change by a different route, and this is the route that runs today: 17.5447511436 sits 1.1092 from gt_value, against pass_tol 0.9326966176, so the band alone scores it 0 (#483).

stopping.why_not_the_criterion: The criterion this case used to declare -- residualControl p/U/(k|omega) 1e-7 -- is structurally unreachable on this case's own shipped mesh, not merely expensive. Measured to 60000 iterations: Ux, k and omega all reach 1e-9 while Uy sits at 3.5e-4 and p at 7.1e-5, both oscillating rather than descending. residualControl takes the max over a vector's components, so Uy pins U; the channel is cyclic and body-force driven, so Uy is physically ~0 and p is defined only up to a constant. That is #199's plane_poiseuille residual floor. A criterion that can never be met is the same defect as no criterion (#273), so it is deleted rather than loosened: loosening it to something reachable would have moved where the oracle stops, and #294's ruling is that gt_value does not move because a stopping rule changed.
stopping.note: This oracle stops on a fixed iteration budget of 5000 and now says so. Running longer does not buy a better answer here and the measurement is the reason to write that down rather than leave it to the next reader: at 5000 iterations the KPI reads 18.8090941, 0.83% from the published Oden Institute chan590 DNS anchor, and at 60000 it reads 19.099023, 2.39% -- three times further out. BOTH ARE INSIDE THE 5% BAND, so the band says nothing about which stopping rule produced either, which is the structural point #286 and #273 measured across the track. gt_value is the published DNS anchor and is untouched; so are pass_tol, the physics window, the KPI name, the cap and instruction.md.
stopping.cost: Shipped configuration, 5000 iterations, measured under #336 on the domain image at 2 CPU: solve.sh 52 s and the evaluator's strip-and-re-run 51 s, against reproduction_timeout_s = 600 and [agent].timeout_sec = 1800. task.toml's oracle_wall_sec = 116 is from the calibration host and is deliberately left alone. THE 664 s FIGURE CARRIED IN #278's COST SURVEY AND IN #294 IS THE 60000-ITERATION REACHABILITY PROBE, a run this case does not perform; reading it as this case's cost is what put this case on an over-budget list.
stopping.measured_on: sim-benchmark-cfd-fullstack:latest (ESI OpenFOAM v2412), 2 CPU. Residual trajectories and the 60000-iteration probe from #286 / #300; the shipped-configuration cost, the positive control (reward 1.0) and the bit-identical 18.8090941 after the residualControl block was deleted, from #336.

source.data_source: Official Oden Institute MKM DNS file chan590/profiles/chan590.means, associated with Moser, Kim and Mansour (1999), Physics of Fluids 11(4):943-945. File header Re_tau=587.19; 129 half-channel rows. SHA-256 at provenance review: 878bc951794516b6136912f8f098cd6f2f96c4bbe7f21a8cea657ffb270d419d.
source.reference_value: U_b/u_tau = 18.653932352, derived by trapezoidal integration of Umean (column 3, normalized by u_tau) with respect to y/delta (column 1) over the official 129-point half-channel profile.
source.physics_note: For a fully-developed symmetric channel, U_b/u_tau is the half-channel integral of U+ over y/delta. The official chan590 profile gives 18.653932352 and, with Re_tau=587.19 from its header, a derived half-height bulk Reynolds number of about 10953.4. In the task setup delta=1 and u_tau=1, so U_b/u_tau equals the height-averaged Ux directly.

profile_reference.name: Moser-Kim-Mansour chan590 DNS mean U+
profile_reference.derivation: Linear interpolation of Umean/u_tau from the official half-channel file at eta=1-|y/delta|; mirrored across the centerline to match evaluator_sampleDict.
profile_reference.scoring_status: not_scored -- retained as provenance. tests/spec.json declares one KPI, ub_over_utau, and the evaluator scores that column alone; the weight and thresholds below are the calibration record from 2026-07-19, not a live scoring component (#483).
profile_reference.threshold_source: T_good is above the worst profile RMSE (0.4042 U+) across the three valid wall-resolved calibration grids. T_bad=1.0 U+ is a conservative rejection boundary; values between decay linearly.

ub_over_utau.description: Bulk-mean velocity normalised by the friction velocity, U_b/u_tau, for fully-developed turbulent plane-channel flow at friction Reynolds number Re_tau=590, computed with k-omega SST. U_b is the height-average of the streamwise velocity over the full channel height; u_tau is fixed to 1 by the specified uniform body force. The external V&V anchor is derived from the official Moser-Kim-Mansour chan590 DNS mean profile.
ub_over_utau.pass_tol_source: Flat 5% of |gt_value| — the single band every live track carries (#190, after #188 set it for combustion and battery). The band exists to catch a wrong configuration, not to grade numerical precision, and scoring inside it is binary. Unchanged in value — this case already carried 5%. gt is a dataset-derived DNS anchor from the official Moser-Kim-Mansour chan590 mean profile; the oracle lands 0.65% away. The band is above the worst bulk-value error measured across the three valid wall-resolved calibration grids (0.3045 absolute), so it is not scoring wall-resolution noise the task leaves free. An earlier version of this note said values between the two thresholds decay linearly; they do not — scoring inside the band has been binary since #188.
ub_over_utau.kpi_quality_note: The evaluator strips every artefact the submission shipped -- results.csv included -- re-runs its Allrun from a clean copy, requires that rerun to leave a serialised polyMesh and a solved time directory (has_mesh_and_solution), and reads the ub_over_utau column of the results.csv that rerun wrote. That is the whole of it: what this note used to describe was the pre-#211 native evaluator, and openfoam_interface replaced it without the note following (#483).
ub_over_utau.gt_value_source: Dataset-derived DNS anchor from the official Oden Institute chan590.means file (URL and SHA-256 recorded above), with acceptance thresholds calibrated on three valid OpenFOAM kOmegaSST grids on 2026-07-19.
